surfaces.part: teal tiled roof plane (left and centre columns)
framed opening with cream and blue panel (right side)

answer.evidence: This is a 16x16 kit cell. At x=4 and x=8 the columns repeat a tile course: a light highlight row (1, 9, 13), a mid row, then dark rows (3-4, 6-8, 11-12). These repeating courses read as a sloped tiled roof plane, which is evidence (c). The right side (x=11) has a dark frame at rows 5-6 and 12-13 around a cream and blue panel at rows 7-11. That panel is a vertical front face of about 9 rows. The roof is a tile plane, not a flat band, and a front face is present. The cell is a fragment of a larger structure, so the call is moderately confident.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a single tiny teal tile-sized object, about 16px across, with a small white or cream element. It has no roof, walls, door or windows, so it is not a whole building and does not match the references (the timber-frame house and the stone house with tiled roofs). The measured facts are not bad: 11 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted. But at this size there is no multi-material structure to compare. The roof tile scallops, per-tile highlights, plaster speckle and stone-by-stone shading of the references are absent, and there is only about 3 visible steps on the teal body. Judged by eye it reads as a flat icon or sticker next to the references, and it cannot stand in for a building at this scale. When in doubt, fail.

surfaces.part: window or dormer opening with cream and blue glass on the right side

answer.evidence: This is a fragment of a larger structure, so the call is uncertain. At x=4 and x=8 the column scan repeats the same course pattern every 4 rows: rows 1, 5, 9 and 13 are light (L=168 or 134), then mid, then dark (rows 4 and 12, L=48 and 74). That is stacked roof-tile courses, each with a lit top edge and a shaded lower edge. They fill the full 16-wide silhouette from row 0 to row 15, so the main body is a sloped roof plane (evidence c). The right side (x=11) has a recessed opening: dark rows 5-6, a cream face with a tan top edge at rows 7-11, and dark outline at rows 12-13. That opening is a vertical face about 7 rows tall, which gives the front face. No isometric side face is drawn.

answer.evidence: The cell is a full 16x16 opaque tile with no transparent rows. Columns x=4 and x=8 repeat a 4-row tile course (light 168, mid 134, darker 102, darkest 48-74) from row 1 to row 15, which reads as a sloped roof or tile plane. There is no eave line with shadow and no vertical south face under it. The right side (x=11) has a dark border at rows 0-6, a cream and blue inset at rows 7-11 and a dark strip at rows 12-13, then roof tiles again at rows 14-15. The inset may be a small window, but it is not a front face under the roof, so the cell reads as a flat tiled fill rather than a roof over a front wall.

answer.evidence: The cell is a full 16x16 fragment with no transparent rows. Columns x=4 and x=8 show repeating tile courses: a light row (L=168), mid-tone rows (134, 102), then a dark shadow row (L=48 at row 4, L=74 at row 12), repeating at rows 1, 5, 9 and 13. These read as a sloped roof or awning plane (evidence c). At x=11 the dark line at row 2 and the 2 eave-shadow rows (5-6, L=68) sit above a cream-and-blue panel at rows 7-11, which is a vertical face. A dark base band at rows 12-13 and a teal course at rows 14-15 sit below it. The roof and top slope dominate, and a small vertical front face is present, so this reads as three-quarter. It is a fragment of a larger structure, which makes the call less certain.
